# Command-Line Reference

The help text of `xsh` and every `xsht` command, as the binaries print it.
`docs/SPEC.md` §16 describes what the commands guarantee.

## `xsh`

```text
Usage:
  xsh SCRIPT [ARGS...]
  xsh -- SCRIPT ARGS...
  xsh --startup
  xsh --help

--startup boots the interpreter and exits immediately, running no program. It
exposes the fixed startup cost for benchmarking (e.g. as a calibration baseline).
Use `xsh -- SCRIPT ARGS...` when SCRIPT begins with `-`.
```

## `xsht`

```text
Usage:
  xsht <COMMAND> [OPTIONS]
  xsht -h | --help
  xsht <COMMAND> -h | --help
  xsht help [COMMAND]

Start here:
  Validate source    xsht check [PATH...]
  Format source      xsht fmt [FILE...]
  Improve source     xsht lint [FILE...]
  Inspect syntax     xsht ast SCRIPT
  Highlight source   xsht highlight SCRIPT
  Expand sugar       xsht desugar SCRIPT
  Read the grammar   xsht grammar 
  Run with tracing   xsht trace SCRIPT [ARGS...]
  Query the API      xsht api [QUERY...]
  Run tests          xsht test [FILTER]
  Search source      xsht grep PATTERN [FILE...]
  Rewrite source     xsht refactor PATTERN REPLACEMENT [FILE...]
```

### `xsht check`

```text
xsht check — Parse and type-check scripts

Usage:
  xsht check [--summary] [--annotate[=default|signatures|locals|all|CLASS,...]] [PATH...]

  --summary            Append diagnostic counts by code
  --annotate[=POLICY]  Apply inferred annotations in place
```

### `xsht fmt`

```text
xsht fmt — Format scripts

Usage:
  xsht fmt [--check] [FILE...]

  --check  Check formatting without rewriting
```

### `xsht lint`

```text
xsht lint — Run quality checks and optional fixes

Usage:
  xsht lint [--fix] [--runless] [--only RULE[,RULE...]] [FILE...]
  xsht lint --list [--format text|jsonl]

  --fix                  Apply safe autofixes
  --only RULE[,RULE...]  Report and fix only the named lint codes
  --runless              Reject external commands unless configured
  --list                 List every selectable code with a summary
  --format FORMAT        text or jsonl, with --list
```

### `xsht ast`

```text
xsht ast — Print parser debug output

Usage:
  xsht ast SCRIPT
```

### `xsht highlight`

```text
xsht highlight — Print syntax highlighting runs as JSON Lines

Usage:
  xsht highlight SCRIPT

  Each line is {"kind":KIND,"text":TEXT}; the texts concatenate to the file.
  KINDs: plain, comment, doc-comment, keyword, constant, type, function,
    property, variable, string, path, regex, number, operator, punctuation,
    interpolation.
```

### `xsht desugar`

```text
xsht desugar — Print a script with every sugar form expanded

Usage:
  xsht desugar SCRIPT

  Each sugar statement, such as `repeat N times { ... }` or `return x when c`,
    is replaced by the core statements that define it, with its comments.
  The output is formatted XSH on stdout. SCRIPT is not modified and not
    checked: the output checks when SCRIPT does.
```

### `xsht grammar`

```text
xsht grammar — Print the language grammar

Usage:
  xsht grammar [--format ebnf|json]

  --format FORMAT  ebnf productions (the default) or the json reference that make docs renders
```

### `xsht trace`

```text
xsht trace — Run a script with trace output

Usage:
  xsht trace [--raw] [--trace-format text|jsonl|flamegraph]
             [--trace-file PATH] [--syscalls] [--trace-top-syscalls N]
             SCRIPT [ARGS...]

  --raw                   Write per-event trace output
  --trace-format FORMAT   text, jsonl, or flamegraph
  --trace-file PATH       Write trace output to PATH
  --syscalls              Include native syscall totals
  --trace-top-syscalls N  Show N syscall rows; default: 8
```

### `xsht api`

```text
xsht api — Query language and standard-library metadata

Usage:
  xsht api [OPTIONS] [QUERY...]

  Queries:
    summary | module:NAME | api:MODULE.FUNCTION
    method:RECEIVER.METHOD | record:NAME | language:ID | search:TERMS

  --format FORMAT    text or jsonl
  --strict           Fail when a selector has no match
  --details LEVEL    basic or full
  --query-file PATH  Read selectors from a file
  --stdin            Read selectors from stdin
```

### `xsht test`

```text
xsht test — Run discovered tests

Usage:
  xsht test [OPTIONS] [FILTER]

  --list              List matching tests
  --exact             Match FILTER exactly
  --cov               Print source coverage
  --api               Include API coverage, with --cov
  -j, --jobs N        Run N tests concurrently (default: half the CPUs)
  --timeout DURATION  Fail a test that runs longer (default: 120s; 0 or none disables)
  --nocapture         Show test output
  --fail-fast         Stop after the first failure
  --keep-temp         Preserve temporary directories
  --cov-json FILE     Write coverage JSON
```

### `xsht grep`

```text
xsht grep — Search scripts with AST patterns

Usage:
  xsht grep PATTERN [FILE...]

  Uppercase identifiers are expression metavariables; ARGS.. matches zero or more arguments.

  Examples:
    xsht grep 'X.len()' .
    xsht grep 'X.push(ITEM)' src/
    xsht grep 'M.set(K, V)' .
    xsht grep 'for NAME in ITER' .
```

### `xsht refactor`

```text
xsht refactor — Rewrite scripts with AST patterns

Usage:
  xsht refactor [--dry-run] PATTERN REPLACEMENT [FILE...]

  --dry-run  Show changes without modifying files
```

### Common workflows

```text
  xsht check .
  xsht fmt --check .
  xsht lint --fix .
  xsht test --cov
```
